title: Japan, Dec 2026 · 8 friends
brief:
# Trip brief

I will be in Tokyo 15–19 Dec, Hakone 19–21, Osaka 21–26 (Osaka base, but during the day we will
commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed, ending the night/nightlife in Osaka; if there are cool nightlife
things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them), then Tokyo again 26–29 Dec 2026.

We land at Haneda Terminal 3 on Tue 15 Dec around 15:00 and fly home from Haneda Terminal 3 on
Tue 29 Dec at 17:20.

We are a group of 8, all around 20 years old, all Asian. We love to drink, and we want to maximise
all the time we've got in the country. Think about things like Round1, shopping, and so on; we love
to do it all. No go-karts. Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes.

Stays (already booked): Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara,
Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo).

## What would make this trip legendary

We are eight degenerates, and the goal is the story we tell on the flight home, not a box ticked.
A great day here has one moment nobody else we know has done, with good food and drinks around it.
We already wrote a plan ("Plan C", in data/japan-plan-c.md) that is the real us. Treat it as the
spine: keep what survives checking, and replace what does not with something equally special.

Anti-goals. Nothing that is only there because it is on page one of "Tokyo itinerary" or "Kyoto in
a day". No sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments. No nightclubs (a group rule from
Plan C; ignore touts and "bar" invites in Kabukichō). No go-karts.

Be bold. Prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things (private rooms, a
table for 8, events that only happen on these dates). For every hard-to-book thing, name a safe
fallback beside it so a sold-out ticket does not wreck the day.

## Set pieces (each is a wish; place them on the dates that work)

- Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka.
- The Grand Santa Parade in Umekita, Osaka (about 500 Santas, suits provided and yours to keep; Plan C had it on Tue 22 Dec). Needs a sign-up.
- Pro wrestling: Pro Wrestling NOAH "Thanksgiving 2026" at Korakuen Hall (Plan C had Fri 18 Dec).
- A B.LEAGUE basketball game, Tokyo Sunrockers at Toyota Arena Tokyo (Plan C had Sun 27 Dec).
- A yakatabune dinner cruise with unlimited drinks on Sat 26 Dec, the night of the Odaiba fireworks.
- Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days.
- Yunessun wine, sake and coffee baths in Hakone, and a special group dinner out on the Hakone night (no cooking at the villa).
- A KFC Christmas party barrel on Christmas Eve.
- Fugu in Osaka.
- Morning sumo practice at a stable (Plan C: Arashio-beya in Ryōgoku) and a private omakase counter.
- A 24-hour onsen night (Thermae-yu in Kabukichō or Spa World in Shinsekai).

## How we like to travel

Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote
and tax-free hauls, arcades, karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan) and Round1. Izakaya
and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly. Keep the long
nights, but not every night: at most two deliberate nights under 4 hours' sleep, and any early start
the day after a late night needs a reason (rope-drop at USJ, the first Fushimi Inari light). Everyone
stays together, and every booking says "8名で、同じテーブル/個室".

Never book, pay or post anything. Every booking becomes a to-do with a due date and how to do it.

guide.story: Shirakawa is a short stretch of canal lined with willows and wooden teahouses, with little Tatsumi Bridge and its shrine in the middle. The glow comes from the teahouse lanterns and street lamps, not a festival, and on a December night it's cold, quiet and almost too pretty to be real.
how: From Kawaramachi, cross the Shijō bridge into Gion and find Tatsumi-bashi.
Group photo on the bridge, then walk the canal.
Cut down Hanamikoji and over Shijō-ōhashi into Pontochō, a 9-minute walk.
tips: People live in these teahouses, so keep the noise way down.
Don't chase or close-up photograph geiko or maiko.

Order your last drinks before the 20:30 last order.

Do two rounds. Beers are about ¥500–700 and cocktails about ¥800–1,200.

guide.story: Itsukushima Shrine is built out over the water on stilts, and its huge vermilion torii stands in the bay. Today you get a spring tide with high water at 09:29, so the gate rises straight out of the sea instead of out of the mud. The cold winter air off the water keeps it sharp, and the deer don't care about any of it.
how: The 08:59 JR ferry from Miyajimaguchi lands at 09:09 (on the pass), just before high water.
Walk the shoreline to the shrine and pay ¥300 to walk the corridors over the water.
Take the group shot of the torii from the shore while the tide is in.
tips: The torii is in the water roughly 07:30–11:30 today, so don't dawdle on the island.
Take the JR ferry. It's the one the pass covers.

Graze the street stalls for more grilled oysters and fresh momiji manjū.
Take the 12:37 JR ferry back, then the JR Sanyo line to Nishi-Hiroshima and the Hiroden tram to Dobashi.

guide.story: The Peace Memorial Museum shows what happened on 6 August 1945 through ordinary things: clothes, a tricycle, a melted lunchbox. how: Buy WEB tickets ahead (¥200), because same-day tickets can take a while.
Walk through the permanent exhibits, then out to the Cenotaph and the Flame of Peace.

how: It opens at 16:00 and there are no reservations. The plan gets you there at 16:40, so send two people ahead from the Dome to hold a place in the queue.
Expect to sit as two tables of four.
Eat from the teppan with the spatula, not a plate.
tips: Wednesday is fine: it closes Mondays and the 1st/3rd Tuesday.

logistics: Luggage, Dec 15–18: everything comes from Haneda to Ninja House (Toshima).

Luggage, Fri 18 Dec: send the big suitcases with Yamato TA-Q-BIN (konbini or front desk) to Kujō House for Mon 21 evening delivery (confirm the host can receive them). Take only overnight bags to Hakone on Dec 19; they ride along to Odawara, Kyoto and Osaka on Dec 21.

Luggage, Fri 25 Dec: send the suitcases from Kujō House to Garfield House (Shinjuku) by TA-Q-BIN for Sat 26 evening delivery (confirm the host can receive them). Dec 26 travel with overnight bags only.
Luggage, Sun 27 Dec: send the big suitcases from Garfield House to Haneda T3 with Yamato airport delivery so Tue 29 Dec is bag-free until the airline bag drop.

Passes: Hakone Freepass (from Shinjuku, Dec 19–20) covers the Odakyu base fare to Hakone-Yumoto, the Tozan trains and buses, ropeway, the pirate ship and discounts at the Open-Air Museum and Glass no Mori. The Romancecar itself needs a separate limited-express ticket (about ¥1,200). The JR Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass (¥17,000 adult, five consecutive days) should start on Tue 22 Dec (Kyoto by JR) and run to Sat 26 Dec: it covers the Hiroshima day on Dec 23 (Nozomi, Mizuho, Sakura and Hikari are all covered between Shin-Osaka and Hiroshima, per JR West), USJ by JR on Dec 24 and Nara on Dec 25, but not the Tokaido Shinkansen to Tokyo on Dec 26. Dec 21 (Odawara to Kyoto on the Tokaido Shinkansen) is outside the pass.
Transit cards: Welcome Suica on the phone covers Tokyo and, as an IC card, Osaka and Kyoto trains and buses as well. Load enough for a few days so nobody holds up a gate.

Money: pay in yen (decline pay in USD); carry about ¥10,000 cash each for markets, small izakaya, the flea markets and cash-only ramen. Tax-free shopping is a refund system: keep the passports with you at every shop, spend ¥5,000 or more per shop per day, and finish the paperwork at the Haneda T3 customs kiosk before bag drop on Dec 29.
Ages and ID: the drinking age is 20 and some places refuse under-20s (Umi no Ie in Shinjuku, some Round1 night rules). Carry the original passports every night.

Year-end: many shops and attractions shorten or close from Dec 29. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government observatory is closed on both sides on Dec 29 and the north side on Dec 28, so use it on Dec 27 if at all. Odaiba Rainbow Fireworks are on Sat Dec 26 at 19:00 (cancelled in bad weather).

Unconfirmed event items to re-check before spending: Pro Wrestling NOAH Thanksgiving 2026 on Dec 18 (tickets expected mid-November), the Tokyo Sunrockers game on Dec 27 and the Kawasaki–Chiba game (fixtures not on any official page yet), live sumo practice at Arashio-beya on Dec 17 (the winter sumo tour at Hasuda is Dec 16), and the Santa Parade sign-up (opens early November).
